verdict.rationale: Tavily's core operations take natural-language input. Search, QnA and research accept plain-English questions, crawl accepts natural-language `instructions`, and the `tvly` CLI takes free-text queries. The official MCP server lets users drive Tavily conversationally from Cursor, Claude Desktop or any MCP client, and a SKILL.md lets a coding agent install and configure it. Missing for 10: the documented MCP tools cover only search and extract (not crawl, map or research), there is no evidence of natural-language control over account or usage management, and nothing independent or hands-on corroborates the natural-language operation.
